newsitem.title: POLAND: Bank wants Espebepe to change debt plan.
newsitem.headline: Bank wants Espebepe to change debt plan.

text.p: Poland's Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBKS), one of the main creditors of the debt-ridden Espebepe SA construction firm, said the company's current debt restructuring plan was unacceptable.

PBKS, which is a part of the state-owned banking group led by Pekao SA, said in a Thursday statement Espebepe's proposal of a 95-percent debt write-off stood no chance of being accepted during the company's creditors meeting on April 14. @

"Pomorski Bank Kredytowy is not interested in Espebepe's bankruptcy, on the contrary it would like to help the firm recover but PBKS cannot accept the Espebepe proposal which assumes a 95-percent reduction of its debts," it said.
"A debt write-off of such a scale in our opinion stands no chance of being accepted at the Monday creditors meeting," it added.
PBKS reiterated its earlier proposal that the debt restructuring be combined with a debt-for-equity swap through a convertible bond issue. @

But Espebepe, burdened with about 75 million zlotys in debt, has so far rejected PBKS' plan as too time-consuming and has said that only a very deep cut in its dues to main creditors could save the company from bankruptcy.
